evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: During the review, we’ll check that your app follows the guidelines below, which you’ll see summarized when you submit your app.
evidence.answer: Apps are checked during a Slack Marketplace review before listing; the review checks that the app follows the guidelines.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Your app being approved is only the beginning!
evidence.answer: Approval is needed for a Marketplace listing; being approved is described as only the beginning of ongoing requirements.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: In addition to the above, if you’re requesting scopes that provide extensive access to workspace data or allow the bot to add itself to private conversations, your submission will be subject to an enhanced review, to reduce the risk of unexpected behavior.
evidence.answer: Triggered only when the app requests extensive-access or private-conversation scopes: the submission gets an enhanced review.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: If your app connects an MCP server to the Slackbot MCP client , the Marketplace team will evaluate additional areas in addition to the standard review criteria above.
evidence.answer: Apps connecting an MCP server to the Slackbot MCP client get extra Marketplace evaluation beyond the standard review criteria.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Our team may also perform an advanced security review at any point after an app is submitted to the Slack Marketplace.
evidence.answer: Slack may run an advanced security review at any time after submission (not limited to specific triggers).

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: As part of reviewing your submission to the Slack Marketplace we will install and test your Slack app to assess the user experience; below are some of the things we will be looking for.
evidence.answer: Slack Marketplace apps are reviewed by installing and testing them; the page does not state a user or install count that avoids review.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: We are unlikely to approve use of admin* scopes by apps submitting to the Slack Marketplace who are not part of our partner program
evidence.answer: Unlikely to approve admin.* scopes for apps that are not part of Slack's partner program.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: As installation of your Slack app will be accessible to anyone with a Slack workspace who views your Slack Marketplace listing, your onboarding flow needs to account for this.
evidence.answer: With direct install enabled, anyone with a Slack workspace who views the Marketplace listing can install the app, so the listing is the access point.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: As part of reviewing your submission to the Slack Marketplace we will install and test your Slack app to assess the user experience; below are some of the things we will be looking for.
evidence.answer: The review installs and tests the app to assess user experience, looking at the items listed in the guide.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Apps that do not follow these terms will not be accepted in the Slack Marketplace.
evidence.answer: The review checks that the app is suitable for the Marketplace and follows the listed policies; apps not following the terms are not accepted.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: DO provide clear reasons for each of the scopes you include in your submitted app.
evidence.answer: The developer must give a clear reason for each requested scope, explaining how the app uses it rather than what the scope does.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: DO disclose the following AI-related information in the relevant fields in the Security & Compliance section of your submission:
evidence.answer: The developer must provide AI details in the Security & Compliance section of the submission when the app exposes users to an LLM: model used, data retention and use by the LLM, LLM data tenancy and LLM data residency.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Use a .jpg, .jpeg, or .png file format, and make sure the size is under 2MB.
evidence.answer: Listing must include app images at 1600px by 1000px (8:5 ratio); images must be .jpg, .jpeg, or .png and under 2MB.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Please note: if the image is low quality (blurry or with an incorrect aspect ratio) or completely unrelated to your app, we will return your submission.
evidence.answer: Apps must include app images in their listings; low-quality or unrelated images lead to the submission being returned.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Make sure to keep it short and sweet at 10 words (or fewer) so that it doesn’t get cut off anywhere.
evidence.answer: Short description must be 10 words or fewer.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Make sure your video is publicly-accessible YouTube link, not a link to a channel or playlist.
evidence.answer: A video is strongly recommended (not stated as required); if provided, it should be 30-90 seconds and a publicly accessible YouTube link, not a channel or playlist.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: There is a clear way to get in touch with your support if someone needs help, such as an email address or contact form.
evidence.answer: The support page must give a clear way to get in touch, such as an email address or contact form, and support requests are expected to get a response within 2 business days.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: We expect support requests to receive a response within 2 business days
evidence.answer: Support requests are expected to receive a response within 2 business days.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: All Slack Marketplace apps must include a clear privacy policy that details how third-party data is handled and this page should be accessible on your app’s landing page.
evidence.answer: Every app must have a privacy policy page accessible from the landing page, covering how third-party data is handled.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: At a minimum should be an email address or a webform.
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must provide an email address or webform for data requests; a physical address alone is not sufficient.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: your app must use the state parameter when requesting access to customer data during the OAuth flow
evidence.answer: The app must use the OAuth state parameter when requesting customer data.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Before your server responds to a request, you must verify that any requests received at these endpoints are authentic by using signed secrets or mutual TLS
evidence.answer: Requests to the app's endpoints must be verified using signed secrets or mutual TLS, not the deprecated verification tokens.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Your app must store API tokens securely.
evidence.answer: API tokens must be stored securely and never logged, stored in client-side code or public repositories, or made accessible to end users.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: your landing page needs to be publicly accessible (i.e. not behind a login)
evidence.answer: The landing page must be publicly accessible (not behind a login) and must be an actual web page made for the Slack app, not a PDF, document or code repository link.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: We are unlikely to approve broad access to workspace message/file data (e.g. user token * :history scopes) without a clear use case that requires them, such as Real-time Search or MCP server functionality
evidence.answer: Scopes that give extensive access to workspace message or file data, such as user token *:history, are unlikely to be approved without a clear use case such as Real-time Search or MCP server functionality.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: search:read.* , *:history , files:read , and canvases:read
evidence.answer: Scopes in the enhanced-review group include search:read.*, *:history, files:read, and canvases:read.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: user token groups:write , groups:write.invites , mpim:write
evidence.answer: Scopes in the enhanced-review group include user token groups:write, groups:write.invites, and mpim:write.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: conversations.connect:write
evidence.answer: conversations.connect:write triggers the enhanced review.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: admin.*
evidence.answer: admin.* scopes trigger the enhanced review.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: DON’T request legacy/restricted scopes.
evidence.answer: Apps must not request legacy or restricted scopes; the page links to further details.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: use legacy/restricted scopes or methods, scopes that provide extensive access to workspace data without a clear use case that requires them
evidence.answer: Legacy or restricted scopes or methods, broad workspace-data scopes without a clear use case, and coded workflow scopes (such as admin.*, identity.*, search:read, workflow.steps:execute, triggers:*) make an app unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Focus on requesting the smallest number of least permissive scopes you can while still providing a good experience.
evidence.answer: Developers should follow least privilege and request the fewest, least permissive scopes that still give a good experience.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: DON’T include scopes in your submitted app intended for future functionality.
evidence.answer: Scopes intended for future functionality must not be included; only scopes for functionality Slack can test are approved.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Scopes marked as required are always included; scopes marked as optional can be accepted or declined by the user without blocking installation.
evidence.answer: Optional scopes can be accepted or declined by the user at install time without blocking installation; required scopes are always included.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Your app should be fully usable with only its required scopes
evidence.answer: Scopes required for core functionality must not be marked optional; the app must be fully usable with only its required scopes.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: To enable this you will need to request the team.billing:read bot token scope, which will enable you to check the workspace plan post-authorization and revoke it if needed.
evidence.answer: Automation platform apps must request the team.billing:read bot token scope to check the workspace plan after authorization.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: We will return submissions where user token scopes are being used unnecessarily.
evidence.answer: User token scopes are returned in review if used unnecessarily.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: are in private beta, still being built, or have not been fully tested.
evidence.answer: Apps that are not in private beta, still being built, or not fully tested are required for Marketplace eligibility.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: You must resubmit your app for review when you make substantial changes or updates to the features, purpose or functionality of your app.
evidence.answer: Substantial changes to features, purpose or functionality require a resubmission for review.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: your app's functionality changes substantially without notice and without the app being resubmitted for review.
evidence.answer: Apps whose functionality changes substantially without resubmission can be delisted without prior notice.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Slack allows you to charge users for your app.
evidence.answer: Developers may charge users for their app; if they do, they should handle payments securely and give transparent billing policy information.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: If you do so, you should handle payments securely and provide transparent information on your billing policy.
evidence.answer: If you charge, handle payments securely and provide transparent billing information.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Included with service subscription: the app is free so long as users have a paid plan with your service.
evidence.answer: The pricing model 'Included with service subscription' makes the app free only when users have a paid plan with the developer's service.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Because of this we require that you limit the installation of your app to Slack workspaces on our paid plans.
evidence.answer: Automation platform apps must be installable only in Slack workspaces on paid plans.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: let users know that a paid Slack plan is required to access the AI agent in the app container.
evidence.answer: For apps with the Agent or Assistant UI, customers need a paid Slack plan to access the AI agent in the app container; other features still work on free plans.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: ensure that your app functions as expected on workspaces that are not on a Slack paid plan
evidence.answer: Apps must function on workspaces without a paid Slack plan, where the AI agent container is unavailable.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The URL you provide must HTTP 302 redirect to a fully qualified slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize URL
evidence.answer: A direct install URL must HTTP 302 redirect to a fully qualified slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize URL.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: your app must use TLS version 1.2 or greater to continue using Slack endpoints.
evidence.answer: Apps must use TLS 1.2 or greater to keep using Slack endpoints (required since February 19, 2020).

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your app needs Transport Layer Security (TLS) to encrypt all traffic between clients and servers.
evidence.answer: Apps need Transport Layer Security (TLS) to encrypt all traffic between clients and servers.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Once your app completes the OAuth flow with a Slack workspace, verify that the connecting user's account matches the enterprise customer's expected domain.
evidence.answer: After OAuth completes for an enterprise customer, the app should verify the connecting user's account matches the customer's expected domain.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Open the Basic Information page
evidence.answer: Direct install is set up on the app's Basic Information page under Installing Your App.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Scroll down to Installing Your App
evidence.answer: Scroll to the Installing Your App section on the Basic Information page.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Select and enable Install from Slack Marketplace
evidence.answer: Enable direct install by selecting Install from Slack Marketplace.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Edit your app's collaborator list by going to your app's settings dashboard and clicking into the Collaborators page.
evidence.answer: Collaborators are edited from the Collaborators page in the app's settings dashboard.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If accidentally exposed, you can regenerate it from your app settings.
evidence.answer: The signing secret should be protected like a password and can be regenerated from the app settings if exposed.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: You can remove your published app from the Slack Marketplace in the Published app settings section of your app's settings dashboard.
evidence.answer: Published apps are removed from the Marketplace in the Published app settings section of the app settings dashboard.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: When your app is no longer supported, these API tokens need to be invalidated by deleting your app from your app settings page.
evidence.answer: API tokens are invalidated by deleting the app from the app settings page when the app is no longer supported.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: are installed on less than 10 active workspaces and have less than 10 weekly active users.
evidence.answer: Apps installed on fewer than 10 active workspaces and with fewer than 10 weekly active users are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Active workspaces are workspaces that have been used in the past 28 days (and that are not sandboxes).
evidence.answer: An active workspace is one used in the past 28 days that is not a sandbox.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Note: this does not apply to security & compliance partners working with our Discovery API
evidence.answer: The 10-workspace and 10-weekly-user minimum does not apply to security and compliance partners working with the Discovery API.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: are in private beta, still being built, or have not been fully tested.
evidence.answer: Apps that are in private beta, still being built, or not fully tested are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: replicate Slack client functionality, or are third-party Slack clients.
evidence.answer: Apps that replicate Slack client functionality or are third-party Slack clients are unsuitable.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: use Slack data to train Large Language Models (LLMs).
evidence.answer: Apps that use Slack data to train LLMs are unsuitable for the Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: provide only an MCP server without meaningful in-Slack functionality.
evidence.answer: Apps that provide only an MCP server without meaningful in-Slack functionality are unsuitable.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: In addition, coded workflows are currently not eligible for listing in the Slack Marketplace.
evidence.answer: Coded workflows are currently not eligible for listing in the Slack Marketplace.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The list below is not exhaustive-the Slack Marketplace team may use their judgment to deny any app from being listed.
evidence.answer: The Marketplace team may use judgment to deny any app from being listed; the unsuitable list is not exhaustive.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: By distributing your app through the Slack Marketplace, you agree to abide by the following core policies and terms:
evidence.answer: By distributing through the Marketplace, developers agree to the App Developer Policy, Slack Marketplace Agreement, Security Review, API Terms of Service and Brand Guidelines.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: If your Slack app integrates with another service, include the name of that service in your app name.
evidence.answer: If the app integrates with another service, the service's name must be included in the app name, and trademarks or copyright must not be infringed.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: If you do not own the service, make sure to not infringe on any trademarks or copyright
evidence.answer: Apps not owned by the developer's service must not infringe trademarks or copyright in their names.
